title: Multi-separator extraction — try multiple separators, validate with domain guard
trigger: Structured data (language code, version, episode number) must be extracted from a URL/filename, but different sites use different separator conventions
principle: When extracting structured data from a URL/filename, try multiple separator conventions (., -, _) — different sites use different conventions. Validate each candidate with a domain guard (isValidIsoCode for language, regex for version pattern) to avoid false positives from word fragments. Order: most-specific convention first (dot-split for lang suffix), broader convention second (kebab-split), structural fallback last (folder segment). The domain guard is mandatory — without it, word fragments like 'memories' or 'episode' match the BCP47 2-3 letter shape but are not language codes.

cases.context: Subtitle URL uses kebab-case lang suffix ('episode-1-en.srt') instead of dot-separated ('episode-1.en.srt'); dot-split yields a single segment so the language is missed and auto-load never triggers
Subtitle URL uses a lang-index pattern ('eng-2.vtt') where the last kebab segment is a numeric index, not a language code; both dot-split and kebab-split miss it

applyFor: Version parsing from filenames (file-1-2-3.txt vs file.1.2.3.txt vs file_1_2_3.txt)
Episode/season number extraction (show-s01-e02 vs show.s01e02 vs show_01_02)
Any structured data extraction from URL/filename where sites use different separator conventions
